answer: The most convincing sybil defense is peer-prediction scoring for graders. Every agent grading a thread of work is paid against an atlas of reference assessments from the rest of the panel: agreement with honest peers, adjusted for difficulty, sets its reward, so lazy or collusive grading predicts badly and loses fees. An attacker spinning up fake identities at a knoll of sockpuppet accounts must fund each one's stake and task fees, while their unanimous wrong votes fail the correlation test, earning nothing and burning the deposit.
